correctness.summary: The tree fixed-point equations force geometric weights on every arm and reduce the center constraints to a unique scalar equation. Strict monotonicity in arm length yields the distortion and the sharp fixed-(d,L) extremizers. A standalone numerical verifier checks 660 deterministic spider instances and the stated closed forms.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The current full text of arXiv:2609.12125v2 was inspected: its explicit examples are double stars and a symmetric three-center tree, and it gives ST_{2,1} only as a strict suppression example. Searches for spider, starlike-tree, subdivided-star, uniform-subdivision, and equivalent weighted LLY formulations found no general spider distortion law or stronger coverage. Nearby discrete-Einstein and prescribed-curvature work studies different optimization targets. Very recent unindexed parallel work remains the main residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem solves the new curvature-distortion invariant for every finite spider, gives its canonical optimal weight explicitly, and shows an exponentially sharp subdivision effect: at fixed center degree d and maximum arm length L the distortion ranges from (d-1)^((L-1)/L) to (d-1)^(L-1).

limitations: The theorem concerns finite spider trees in the fixed-combinatorial-distance weighted LLY convention.
General mixed arm lengths are characterized by a unique scalar equation rather than an elementary closed form.
The curvature-distortion literature is extremely recent, so unindexed parallel work remains a residual originality risk.
Finite numerical verification supports but does not replace the proof.
Independent audit has not been performed.
review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
